To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PTEN loss confers resistance to erlotnib-induced apoptosis in NSCLC cells; (2) PTEN loss leads to persistent activation of the AKT–Survivin pathway, which underlies the resistance to erlotninib-induced apoptosis; (3) downregulation of survivn either by siRNA transfection or by exposure to a small-molecule survivn suppressor YM155 reverses erlotinib resitance in NSCLC cell lines

the expression of survivin is upregulated in EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC cells lacking PTEN expression, that this upregulation contributes to erlotinhib resistance, and that the small molecule survivin inhibitor YM155 overcomes erlotinib-resistant growth of such cells in vitro and in vivo.

persistent activation of the AKT– survivin pathway induced by loss of PTEN underlies a mechanism for EGFR–TK I resistance in EGFR mutant NSCLC and that the targeting of the antiapop-totic protein survivin has the po-tential to overcome resistance to EGFR– TKIs in EGFR mutant lung cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of resistance to EGFR–tyrosine kinase inhibitors and the potential for overcoming such resistance in NSCLC.
identifying mechanisms that underlie resistance to EGFR–tyrosine kinase inhibitors and developing new strategies to overcome such resistance.
understanding and overcoming the resistance to epider-mal growth factor receptor (EGR)-tyrosine kinase inhibitors in lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“PTEN loss is a mechanism of acquired resistance to EGFR TKIs in EGFR-mutated NSCLC.
PTEN loss in NSCLC is associated with resistance to EGFR TKI, but that the underlying mechanism is through AKT-survivin signaling, and thus targeting survivin could overcome resistance to EGFR-TKI.
PTEN loss induces resistance to EGFR TKI through activation of the AKT–Survivin pathway, and that targeting survivin has the capacity to overcome this resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel mechanism of resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor-induced apoptosis in EGFER mutation-positive non–small cell cancer.
the targeting of Survivin has the potential in combination with EGFR-TKIs to overcome the EGFR-TKI resistance in EGFR mutant NSCLC.
PTEN loss in EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC cells leads to activation of the AKT-survivin pathway and contributes to resistance to EGFR-TKIs through the suppression of erlotinib–induced apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

targeting the antiapoptosis factor survivin may be a useful strategy for overcoming erlotinib (Tarceva) resistance in non–small cell carcinoma of the lung that has an activating epidermal growth receptor gene mutation and a loss of the tumor-suppressor gene PTEN.
the antiapoptosis protein survivin is a potential target for overcoming EGFR–TKi resistance in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
the targeting of the antiapptotic protein survivin has the ability to overcome erlotinib-resistance in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
